cards.text: Ezra tells this one himself, friend. He's a priest and a scribe skilled in the Law of Moses, and King Artaxerxes of Persia sent him to Jerusalem with silver and gold for God's house (Ezra 7:1, 6, 11-16). Now Ezra writes down the family heads who came with him from Babylon.

Then comes the list of family heads and how many men came with each, including Hattush from the descendants of DAVID. One family head brings 28 men, another brings 300, and Ezra writes it all down like the most serious sign-up sheet in history.

Ezra gathers everybody at the canal that flows to Ahava, and they camp there three days. Then he walks the camp searching among the people and the priests, like a trip leader doing a head count before the bus pulls out.

cards.question: Ezra searches the camp by the Ahava canal. Which group can't he find a single one of?

cards.text: So Ezra sends a team of leaders and teachers to Iddo, the leader at Casiphia, and the name Elnathan shows up THREE times on that team. Somebody yells "Elnathan!" and three heads turn around.

cards.question: Ezra's team carries a message to Iddo and his kinsmen at Casiphia. What are they asked to bring back?

answers.text: Ministers for the house of God
Silver for the house of God

cards.text: The team doesn't come back from Casiphia empty-handed, friend. They come back with LEVITES.

cards.question: Ezra's team comes back from Casiphia with Levites. What does Ezra say is behind it?
First comes Sherebiah, a man of insight from the descendants of Mahli son of Levi, with his sons and brothers, 18 men. True or false: Sherebiah's group is the only group of Levites that comes.
Hashabiah comes too, together with Jeshaiah, and with his brothers and their sons, 20 men. Which line of Levi are they descended from?
They also bring 220 ___ servants, all designated by name. David and the officials had appointed them to assist the Levites.

cards.text: Now they've got their Levites, and the road to Jerusalem is waiting. But Ezra stops everything right there by the Ahava Canal.

cards.question: Ezra wants them to humble themselves before God and ask for a safe journey for their children and all their possessions. So what does he proclaim?

cards.text: Here's the thing. There are enemies on that road, and the easy move is to ask the king for soldiers and horsemen, but Ezra's too ashamed to ask.

cards.question: Why is Ezra ashamed to ask King Artaxerxes for an escort of soldiers?

answers.text: He had told the king his God helps everyone who seeks Him
The king had already turned down his other requests
He knew the king needed every soldier to guard Babylon

cards.text: Think about it. Telling the king "my God's got us" and then asking for spears is like telling your boss "I got this" and calling him from the parking lot for a ride, so instead they fast and petition their God about it.

cards.question: Ezra and the exiles fast and ask God for a safe journey. True or false: God grants their request.

cards.text: Next, Ezra sets apart twelve of the leading priests, plus Sherebiah, Hashabiah and ten of their brothers. He's got a job for them.

cards.question: What does Ezra weigh out into the hands of these priests and Levites?

answers.text: Silver and gold for God's house
Spears and shields for the road
Grain and oil for the altar

cards.text: We're talking 650 talents of silver, 100 talents of gold, 20 gold bowls, and two articles of fine polished bronze as precious as gold. I lose my oven timer twice a day, friend, and NOBODY is ever handing me 100 talents of gold.
Then Ezra looks at the priests and Levites and tells them, "You are holy to the LORD, and these articles are holy."

cards.question: True or false: Ezra says the silver and gold is tax money owed to the king.
Ezra gives the priests and Levites a job until they reach the house of the LORD in Jerusalem. What is it?

cards.text: So the priests and Levites take charge of it all, and on the twelfth day of the first month, they set out from the Ahava Canal. No soldiers. No horsemen. Just families walking toward Jerusalem with a FORTUNE in gold.

cards.question: Ezra's group heads for Jerusalem with no escort. What happens on the road?

answers.text: God protects them from enemies and bandits
Bandits steal part of the silver
The king's soldiers catch up to guard them

cards.question: They arrive in Jerusalem and rest there for ___ days.

cards.text: On the fourth day, in the house of God, they hand it all over to Meremoth son of Uriah, the priest. Eleazar son of Phinehas and two Levites are right there beside him.

cards.question: Everything is verified by ___ and ___, and the total is written down right then.

cards.text: Then the exiles who came back from captivity sacrifice burnt offerings to the God of Israel. Rams, lambs, the works.

cards.question: Part of the offering is bulls for all Israel. How many bulls?
True or false: Along with the rams and lambs, the exiles bring a sin offering of 12 male goats.

cards.text: They also hand the king's edicts to the royal satraps and governors west of the Euphrates. Paperwork, delivered.

cards.question: Once the satraps and governors get King Artaxerxes's edicts, what do they do?

answers.text: Assist the people and the house of God
Demand tribute from the priests and Levites
Send Ezra and his group back to Babylon

cards.text: The gold's delivered and the offerings are made, but hang on, friend. Ezra's story in Jerusalem isn't done yet.

findings.problem: The card says the list gives 'how many men came with each' family head. That is not true of the whole list. Gershom, Daniel and Hattush (Ezra 8:2) are named with no count of men.

rule.text: Noticing: What he points out must be true.

findings.problem: The wrong answers 'Singers' and 'Gatekeepers' are never shown false in this passage. The passage never says any singers or gatekeepers were found at the Ahava canal. Singers and gatekeepers also served alongside the Levites, so a baker could argue that none of them were there either.

rule.text: Each wrong answer must be false anywhere in the passage, not just at that moment.

findings.problem: Nothing on the earlier cards lets the baker reason out whether Sherebiah's group is the only group of Levites that comes. The answer is a coin flip.

rule.text: The check: could a thoughtful baker who has only seen the earlier cards make a reasoned pick? If the only way to get it right is luck, give the story card more context or ask a different question.

findings.problem: Asking which line of Levi Hashabiah's group comes from (Merari, Kohath or Gershon) is trivia. It doesn't move the passage forward, the baker doesn't need it to understand the passage, and it can only be guessed. It also comes right after the coin-flip card 9.

rule.text: Ask about the moments that move the passage forward and the details the baker needs to understand it.

findings.problem: Multiple choice dominates stop 1. It has 6 multiple choice cards, 2 true or false cards and 1 fill in the blank card. Cards 4, 6 and 8 are multiple choice three times in a row.

rule.text: No formula. Which question type comes next, the order the types come in and where a blank falls are chosen naturally for each card. They never follow a pattern. No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: This story card has four sentences: the long first sentence, 'No soldiers.', 'No horsemen.' and 'Just families walking...'.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The wrong answer 'value' is close to the right answer 'weight'. The silver and gold were checked by weight, which sets their value, and the passage itself uses 'valued' for the gold bowls (Ezra 8:27). A baker could argue it's right.

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: The card assigns 'number' to blank 1 and 'weight' to blank 2. Nothing lets the baker reason out which word comes first, so the order tests wording the baker hasn't seen.

rule.text: The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The card opens with a recap ('The gold's delivered and the offerings are made') and cites Ezra 8:36 without telling anything from that verse. Card 15 already told it and card 16 asked about it. The card should be only the story-isn't-over line.

Papa Dorin's voice goes flat through most of stop 2. Cards 1, 4, 10 and 12 tell the passage with no humor or personality, and card 15 has only a small dry line. The treasure handover, the unescorted road and the arrival in Jerusalem are moments that could hold a real laugh without muddying a fact.

rule.text: When a moment can hold a real laugh without muddying a fact, he goes for it. If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.
